claims.text: Anthropic measured five MCP servers at 58 tools and about 55,000 tokens of tool definitions before any work started (Anthropic, 24 Nov 2025).

Tool-count guidance by vendor: OpenAI recommends fewer than 20 functions at the start of a turn, Google recommends 10 to 20 active tools, Anthropic says selection accuracy degrades past 30 to 50 tools, and Microsoft 365 Copilot warns quality may degrade beyond 10 functions.
Every vendor's answer to tool-count limits is tool search, where tools are marked for deferred loading and the model searches for the ones it needs.

The MCP specification 2026-07-28 is stateless: no initialize handshake and no Mcp-Session-Id header; each request carries protocol version, client capabilities and client identity in _meta, and a mandatory server/discover call advertises server support.
In MCP 2026-07-28, each POST carries Mcp-Method and Mcp-Name headers so gateways can route without parsing the body.
MCP 2026-07-28 deprecated dynamic client registration, roots, sampling, logging and HTTP+SSE, and moved tasks into an extension, with a 12-month deprecation policy.
MCP 2025-06-18 made the server an OAuth resource server with protected resource metadata and required resource indicators; 2025-11-25 recommended Client ID Metadata Documents for client registration.

Invariant Labs described tool poisoning, rug pulls (descriptions changed after approval) and cross-server shadowing on 1 Apr 2025; the recommended mitigation is pinning tool lists and treating descriptions and annotations such as readOnlyHint as untrusted input.

On 26 May 2025 Invariant Labs showed a malicious public GitHub issue steering an agent using the official GitHub MCP server into leaking private repository data via a public pull request; no server patch fixes it because the danger comes from combining private data, untrusted input and an outbound channel.
CVE-2025-6514 (mcp-remote, CVSS 9.6) allowed a malicious server to execute commands on Windows, and CVE-2025-49596 (MCP Inspector, CVSS 9.4) let a web page drive an unauthenticated local proxy.
The impostor npm package postmark-mcp 1.0.16 copied every email to an attacker before removal, and Asana's own MCP server exposed data across about 1,000 customers in mid-2025.
The MCP spec forbids token passthrough; the official TypeScript and Python SDKs shipped fixes in October 2026 for bearer authentication that accepted tokens issued for other services.
A Copilot Studio agent shared with maker-provided credentials lets anyone using it act with the maker's access.

The official MCP Registry has been in preview since 8 Sep 2025, stores metadata only, lists no private servers, and its docs warn data resets may occur before general availability; enterprises are expected to run private sub-registries.

Private registry options include Azure API Center, AWS Agent Registry (GA 31 Aug 2026) and Google Agent Registry (GA 18 Jun 2026); gateways include Azure API Management, AgentCore Gateway and Google Agent Gateway.
Pinned tool lists are available via Anthropic's mcp-client-2026-09-15 header and a static mcpToolSchema on AgentCore Gateway.
Block said in June 2025 it had built more than 60 internal MCP servers with one risk level per tool and OAuth with minimal scopes.

Stripe's remote MCP server uses OAuth or scoped agent API keys, organisation-wide on/off switches and dashboard confirmation for sensitive actions, and full-access keys stop working on it after 30 Nov 2026.
MCP and A2A are now under the Agentic AI Foundation (MCP since 9 Dec 2025, A2A since 27 Aug 2026); A2A reached version 1.0.0 on 12 Mar 2026.

Client-to-gateway and gateway-to-upstream are two separate OAuth trust relationships; the gateway is the resource server for the client and the OAuth client toward the upstream, and the MCP spec forbids forwarding a client token to an upstream API.
For the gateway-to-MCP-server hop, token pass-through kills audit and on-behalf-of; the recommended pattern is RFC 8693 token exchange with a nested act claim, with mTLS underneath.
Tool-level authorization should move out of each MCP server and into the gateway, where policy can see mcp.tool.name and tool arguments via CEL rules.

In agentgateway, promptGuard attached to an MCP backend is accepted but does nothing; tool output re-enters the model as a role: tool message that built-in request regex skips, so a request webhook on the LLM route is needed to mask or reject tainted tool output.
A gateway can store a definition_hash (sha256 of tool name, description and schema) per registered tool and block or re-request approval when the live definition changes, defending against rug pulls.

The open-source MCP Gateway & Registry uses an nginx data plane and a FastAPI registry control plane, brokers per-user OAuth (3LO/OBO) egress tokens so they never live on laptops, and offers virtual MCP servers aggregating tools with per-tool access control.
